layers.name: REALITY
layers.question: Does modulating target T actually cause endpoint E?
layers.failure: On-target biology conflated with drug pharmacology. The project asks about the first; all evidence is generated by the second.

layers.name: SELECTION
layers.question: Which truths ever get the chance to become evidence?
layers.failure: Study attention, who got dosed, indication and reporting bias. Degree bias and confounding by indication are BORN here -- not in the model.

layers.name: EVIDENCE
layers.question: What have we actually observed?
layers.failure: Undated or unprovenanced edges admitted, making temporal claims unverifiable.

layers.name: ATTRIBUTION
layers.question: Drug-level observation to target-level claim. Which target did it?
layers.failure: Uniform propagation makes the LABEL a function of target degree -- re-importing the exact confound removed at layer 8.
layers.as_data: Evidence as Data -- q vector, leak, crude/adj

layers.name: LABELING RULE
layers.question: How do we interpret the evidence?
layers.failure: Unlabelled silently treated as negative; evidence tiers pooled so the label's meaning cannot be stated.
layers.as_code: Policy as Code -- tier + earned-negative rules

layers.name: DATASET LABEL
layers.question: positive / earned-negative / unlabelled, per tier
layers.failure: Multiaxiality corrupts the label matrix; a PT annotation becomes a false negative at ancestor level.
layers.as_data: Contracts as Data -- versioned label set

layers.name: SPLIT
layers.question: Which labels does the model SEE vs get TESTED on?
layers.failure: Interpolation split behind an extrapolation claim. Same labels + different split = a different scientific claim.

layers.name: MODEL
layers.question: What can the GNN learn from it?
layers.failure: A popularity detector with an excellent AUROC. Degree explains the score; biology does not.
layers.as_data: Metrics as Data -- per-seed, decile, level

layers.name: VERDICT
layers.question: Promote or reject? At what operating point, on what evidence?
layers.failure: A score shipped where a decision was required; no bound on what the model misses.
layers.as_data: Attestation as Data -- signed model card

questions.title: Is there any signal beyond node popularity?
questions.contrast: GNN vs degree-only null (LogisticRegression on log-degree, no biology, no relations)
questions.if_it_ties: The KG encodes study attention, not safety biology. The project returns a negative result -- and that is a real finding.

questions.title: Does the graph help beyond non-graph target features?
questions.contrast: GNN vs tabular GBM / MLP on target annotations only (GTEx expression breadth, gnomAD pLI & LOEUF, protein family, subcellular localisation)
questions.if_it_ties: Graph structure adds nothing. Ship the cheaper tabular model and close the project.

questions.title: Do the relation TYPES carry the signal?
questions.contrast: Relation-aware (R-GCN, CompGCN, HGT) vs relation-agnostic (GraphSAGE, GAT on a collapsed single adjacency)
questions.if_it_ties: Connectivity matters; relationships per se do not. Q3 is the literal research question in the brief -- if a relation-agnostic GNN matches a relation-aware one, the answer to "can relationships be used to predict" is no, only connectivity can.

rungs.name: Base rate
rungs.asks: What does guessing the prior achieve?
rungs.models: A prevalence constant, equivalent to sklearn DummyClassifier(strategy="prior")
rungs.if_not_beaten: Anchors average precision. Anything not beating it is noise.

rungs.name: Degree-only null
rungs.models: sklearn LogisticRegression on log1p(per-relation degree). No biology, no relations, no message passing.
rungs.if_not_beaten: The graph encodes study attention, not safety biology. The project returns a negative result, and that is a real finding.

rungs.name: Non-graph model
rungs.asks: Do target features alone explain performance?
rungs.models: sklearn HistGradientBoostingClassifier and a tabular MLP on target annotations only: GTEx expression breadth, gnomAD pLI and LOEUF, protein family, subcellular localisation. Zero graph structure.
rungs.if_not_beaten: The graph adds nothing. Ship the cheaper tabular model and close the project.

rungs.name: Graph-topology GBM
rungs.models: sklearn HistGradientBoostingClassifier on personalised PageRank to known-risky targets, betweenness, k-core, clustering, degree. Graph-derived, but no learned representation.
rungs.if_not_beaten: A published comparator of this family reached ROC-AUC around 0.71 on target-level safety attrition. That is the bar a GNN must clear.

rungs.name: Shallow KGE
rungs.asks: Does embedding entities suffice, without message passing?
rungs.models: PyKEEN ComplEx and PyKEEN RotatE: relation-typed scoring functions with no neighbourhood aggregation.
rungs.if_not_beaten: Relation-typed embedding is what helps; aggregation is not.

rungs.name: Relation-agnostic GNN
rungs.models: PyG GraphSAGE (SAGEConv) and PyG GAT (GATConv) over a collapsed single adjacency, with edge types deliberately discarded.
rungs.if_not_beaten: The control that isolates relation types. Without it, no claim about relationships can be made at all.

rungs.name: Relation-aware GNN
rungs.models: PyG R-GCN (RGCNConv), CompGCN and PyG HGT (HGTConv), with a degree-offset head and a gradient-reversal adversary.
rungs.if_not_beaten: The difference between this rung and rung 4 IS the research answer. If it is near zero, connectivity matters and relation types do not.

ladder_rule.rule: Every rung runs on the same split, the same negatives, the same endpoints, and at least five seeds with bootstrap confidence intervals. One seed cannot resolve a 0.02 difference in average precision, and most reported wins on biomedical knowledge graphs sit inside that band.

scope_in: Public, open-source KGs only. Open Targets is primary -- it carries the target-safety widget (ToxCast, AOPWiki, ClinPGx).
Hetionet / PrimeKG as secondary graphs, for cross-KG replication of whatever result Open Targets gives.
AstraZeneca BIKG is the architectural reference only -- it is internal and is not usable as data.
